study.scope: Same two-layer GRU and three total-distribution heads, Train histories, initial weights and training budgets; change the observation likelihood and its family-loss targets only. Historical aggregate controls are reevaluated rather than retrained.
observationAssumptions: Positive total demand is distributed uniformly over the active-day simplex.
Active days follow Bernoulli draws conditioned on at least one active day; the existing horizon=1 zero head supplies the inactive-day probability.
Daily stockout observations are treated as noninformative right censoring. This does not establish the actual intraday stockout mechanism or full cross-horizon marginal consistency.
selection: Report all three seeds; never deploy the best Dev seed.
Before a core rollout, seed 42 must lower seven-day CRPS and each exact order-loss ratio (1,3,9) against the retained GRU.
At least two of three seeds must improve seven-day CRPS and mean exact order loss against both the same-seed expanded control and the retained GRU.
Seed 42 one-day CRPS may increase by at most 10 percent against the retained GRU, and seven-day observed 80-percent interval coverage may not decrease.

If these gates pass, measure an actual manager-request rollout with the frozen language constructor. Require lower total loss and no increase in invalid handoffs or unnecessary requests before replacement.
Joint observation NLL alone never justifies replacement. Exact metrics on uncensored periods do not establish latent-demand calibration.
